title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
source: canonical Longest Increasing Subsequence concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of integers. Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence: values picked left to right, each strictly larger than the one before, not necessarily adjacent.
hints: Track, for each value, the longest chain ending exactly there.
A cheaper trick keeps one sorted list: the smallest tail value of an increasing chain of every length.
For each value, binary search that tail list for the first entry not smaller than it and replace it; append when the value extends the longest chain. The list length is the answer.
solution: Patience method: keep a sorted list of the smallest tail of an increasing chain of each length; place each value with a binary search (replace the first larger tail, or append). O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include duplicates, strictly falling arrays, and an already rising array

visible.failNote: later, smaller values can still extend a chain
